title: Module 2 Interpretation Check
intro: Each item gives you a short research situation. Decide what the evidence supports.

items.q: Eight response times (seconds) are 2, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, and 40. The mean is 8.5 and the median is 4.5. Which summary describes a typical response best?
o: The median, because one extreme score pulls the mean upward
The mean, because it uses every score
The mode, because it is largest
Neither, because the data are nominal
items.why: The score of 40 distorts the mean. The median stays near where most responses fall.

items.q: Two classes both have a mean of 75 on a quiz. Class A has SD = 3 and Class B has SD = 12. Which statement is correct?
o: Class A scores are tightly clustered and Class B scores are widely spread
The classes have identical score distributions
items.why: Equal means can hide very different spreads. The standard deviation shows how much scores differ from that mean.

items.q: A teacher adds 5 bonus points to every exam score. What happens to the mean and standard deviation?
o: The mean rises by 5 and the SD is unchanged
The mean is unchanged and the SD rises by 5
items.why: Every score moves up together, so the center moves and the spread does not.

items.q: A histogram has a long tail to the left, and most scores are bunched at the high end. The skew is
items.why: Skew is named for the tail. A long left tail means negative skew, and the mean falls below the median.

items.q: Scores are 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12. A student says the SD is 8 because the mean is 8. The error is
o: Confusing the mean with the SD. Variability must come from deviations from the mean
items.why: The mean is 8, and the SD is about 3.16 (SS = 40, sample variance = 10). The SD measures spread, not center.
